public_catalog_snapshot.description: ecoinvent 3.12 Database ecoinvent is one of the most famous LCA databases in the world, used by more than 5000 organisations worldwide. The database contains international industrial life cycle inventory data on energy supply, resource extraction, material supply, chemicals, metals, agriculture, waste management services, and transport services with currently more than 26000 peer-reviewed datasets in the latest database version 3.12. Further information can be found on the ecoinvent 3.12 Website or in the ecoinvent 3.12 Knowledge Base . The database is very transparent and consistent. Each data set is provided as a unit process and as an aggregated system process. Moreover, since version 3 of the database, processes are provided for three different system models: "Allocation at the point of substitution" (APOS), "Allocation, cut-off by classification" (Cutoff) and "Substitution, consequential, long-term" (Consequential). Furthermore, reports with background information about modelling procedures and assumptions are published. The ecoinvent database is updated annualy, but ecoinvent v2.2 is still in use and therefore also available via Nexus. All recent databases from ecoinvent are implemented for openLCA v2. You can find a webinar on the ecoinvent implementation in openLCA here: ecoinvent 3.11 in openLCA We offer a fully valid ecoinvent licence with full access to the ecoinvent website and with databases adapted to openLCA. For professors at universities defined as low- and lower-middle-income countries, an Educational Multi-User licence can be ordered for free. Which country is defined as such, you can find in the linked document, page 145: World Economic Situation and Prospects 2025

database_groups.description: ecoinvent v3.12 Release Version 3.12 of the ecoinvent database represents a significant update to the world’s most trusted life cycle inventory database. Designed to empower businesses, researchers, and policy-makers, our latest release expands the breadth of our data, offering new insights and enhanced accuracy for various industries. Further information can be found on the ecoinvent 3.12 Website or in the ecoinvent 3.12 Knowledge Base . Three system models of ecoinvent 3.12 are available for openLCA: Cutoff (Allocation, cut-off by classification), APOS (Allocation at the point of substitution) and Consequential (Substitution, consequential, long-term). All databases from ecoinvent v3.12 are implemented for the latest software version openLCA 2.5.0 (openLCA version on the release date) or newer. If you already own a license and want to have an "openLCA version" of the ecoinvent database, select the "License owner" option of the correspondent license type (e.g. single user, educational etc.). This database contains elementary flow mappings to the reference data from openLCA for ecoinvent version 3.11 or earlier. If you are interested in getting the database without reference data, please contact us. From version 3.12 onwards, the elementary flows are without a mapping to the openLCA reference data and keep the same original UUID number (Universally Unique Identifier) as provided by ecoinvent.

database_groups.name: ecoinvent LCIA Methods
database_groups.description: The data packs include the LCIA methods implemented by the ecoinvent centre for the use with ecoinvent v2 and ecoinvent v3 databases. The LCIA methods are included in the ecoinvent databases by default and they can be used to obtain the same LCIA results as the ones that are published by the ecoinvent centre (for example in ecoQuery). Users need to be aware that the ecoinvent methods only contain the characterisation factors for elementary flows that are included (used) in the ecoinvent databases. The ecoinvent methods are not intended to be used with other databases. The elementary flows inside the methods package contain some reference data (UUID numbers) from openLCA to be compatible with the openLCA methods packages. Since version 3.12, the elementary flows all follow the same UUID number as originally provided by ecoinvent.

public_catalog_snapshot.description: PSILCA v4.0.1, released in January 2026, is the latest version of the social LCA database developed by GreenDelta. It contains comprehensive generic inventory information for almost 15,000 industry sectors and commodities, enabling the calculation and assessment of social impacts of products along their life cycles and the identification of social hotspots. If you are a beginner, it is recommended to additionally book the Quick Start Support Package, which includes an introductory 1-hour webinar and four support tickets.

database_groups.name: PSILCA v4.0.1 - Starter & SimaPro
database_groups.description: The Starter type is the basic version of the database. It provides data for every social indicator as risk-assessed elementary flows on the output side. In the Starter variant, the user cannot see the underlying raw values of the risk assessment. Nevertheless, it is possible for the user to change risk levels individually for processes (e.g. from medium risk to high risk). Furthermore, general information about data sources is provided. A relatively high cut-off criterion of 1E-5 is applied in order to reduce the large amount of datasets and accelerate the calculations of impacts. The PSILCA version for SimaPro basically contains the same features as the openLCA Starter variant. However, risk levels cannot be modified and the applied cut-off criterion is 4E-5. Every licence type contains both PSILCA Starter and PSILCA SimaPro.

database_groups.name: PSILCA v4.0.1- Developer
database_groups.description: The Developer variant of PSILCA is the most comprehensive and complete version of the database. It contains all features of the other two types (risk-assessed indicators and raw values) complemented by information about data quality for each process-specific indicator value. Data quality is assessed by 5 indicators, one of it addressing the reliability of the sources and the other four the conformance of the data set. Since June 2017, overall data quality can be calculated for entire product systems. No cut-off criterion is applied to assure the highest possible precision level of the product systems. Despite of its size, it is possible to use the Developer variant on reasonably modern computers because openLCA is adjusted to the amount of datasets. By purchasing a PSILCA Developer licence, the user also has also access to PSILCA Professional, PSILCA Starter and PSILCA SimaPro.

public_catalog_snapshot.description: Introducing cm.chemicals V2.01 2024 by Carbon Minds. This is the most recent version of the cm.chemicals database. cm.chemicals life-cycle data is a large-scale LCI dataset for the environmental assessment of chemicals and plastics. Backed by a consistent, 3rd party certified methodology and annual updates, cm.chemicals covers 1300 chemicals in 190 geographical regions and is a comprehensive data source for ISO 14040/14044 compliant life-cycle assessment studies for chemicals and plastics. Furthermore, the cm.chemicals methodology is compliant with the Together for Sustainability (TfS) guideline as well as UEIL/ATIEL. We offer licenses for more than five packages which are specifically adapted to the use in openLCA. For chemicals or plastics that are not included in the data packages, we also offer data-on-demand. Data-on-demand is also adapted to use in openLCA. The databases uses LCI datasets.

public_catalog_snapshot.description: AGRIBALYSE 3.2 is the French LCI database for the agriculture and food sector provided by ADEME. This updated version, published in 2023, comprises LCIs for 2500 agricultural and food products produced and/or consumed in France, combining a production-based approach and a consumption-based approach. AGRIBALYSE 3.2 is built upon previous versions started since 2013, with contributions from a network of partners including INRAE, the agriculture and agro-food french technical institutes (ACTA-ACTIA), as well as some consultancies (Gingko 21, Sayari, Blonk, Koch Consulting, Evea). For imported products, Agribalyse 3.2 relies on Ecoinvent and WFLDB data. The standard Agribalyse 3.2 database uses ecoinvent data sets and therefore needs a valid ecoinvent license for the download and usage of this version. Update June 2026: We now also offer below a "core" version of Agribalyse 3.2 where all ecoinvent background datasets are removed, so that it can be used for free and without a valid ecoinvent license. Be aware that due to the removal of the ecoinvent background datasets, not all supply chains are closed and need to be linked to the background database of your choice (ecoinvent, BAFU etc.). public_catalog_snapshot.description: The LCA Commons is a database providing US representative LCA data. The >10,000 datasets have been developed by the different US governmental agencies such as USDA, National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), National Agricultural Library (NAL) and US Forest service and have been created with varying modelling perspectives and nomenclature frameworks. The database is available for free on the LCA Collaboration Server (https://www.lcacommons.gov/lca-collaboration/search). The version described here is created by GreenDelta GmbH based on the public version, with the idea to better align the datasets with the openLCA LCIA methods and to create one integrated and more homogeneous database. The database is available as a complete database with the valid repositories that includes the latest updates from LCA Commons 2025.3 including the USLCI 09.2025, the baseline electricity datasets (2025.3, NIST-construction_materials, US Environmental Protection Agency/Construction and Demolition Debris (CDD) Management, US Environmental Protection Agency/Heavy Equipment Operation, US Forest Service Forest Products Laboratory/Forestry and Forest Products, Argonne National Laboratory/Cement and Concrete.

Over 5Mt pigments are produced worldwide with 16% being coloured inorganic ones and 96% inorganic. Half are used in printing, a quarter in architectural paints and the rest to colour textiles, plastics, ceramics, paper, cement, food, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and coatings. This inventory database has 55 pigments including 31 inorganic pigments of 16 different colours from 8 regions and 24 organic pigments of 10 different hues from 5 regions. Inorganic pigments defined by their colourways, properties, chemical formula and synthesis. They generally meet more extreme thermal, physical and chemical demands of exterior performance than organic pigments. Compared to organic pigments most inorganic ones are brighter, more durable and made with simpler technology. Synthetic organic pigments are each defined and characterised by their colourways, properties, synthesis, microstructure, chemical formula and group. The most colourful and durable but least toxic, fugitive and expensive to make are used as colourants.

database_groups.name: LC-Inventories.ch - Biomass-to-liquid fuel production scenario 1
database_groups.description: LCI data from the project RENEW (Renewable fuels for advanced powertrains). In scenario 1 a modelling of a maximized fuel production is made. The supply chain is supposed to be as efficient as possible regarding biofuel production. One of the highest criteria of the evaluation is the ratio of biofuel production to needed agricultural land. The use of hydrogen improves the carbon/hydrogen-ration and thus leads to a higher conversion rate of biomass to fuel. External conventional electricity input into the production system is used in most of the conversion concepts for providing the necessary hydrogen. A quite crucial point in scenario 1 is the assumption on the hydrogen supply for the biomass conversion. For these datasets, it is assumed that the external electricity is provided with wind power plants. It is not realistic to get such a renewable electricity supply until 2020 for more than a small number of conversion plants, but this scenario describe a direction that might be worth going in special locations. This database contains reference data from openLCA. For details, please refer to the FAQs, here . If you are interested in getting the database without reference data, please contact us ( www.openlca.org ).
